prompt.context: Our client is a large national health care payer (health insurance company, think Aetna) exploring the launch of a new disease management ("DM") program to better serve its 5 million members. The idea is to hire and train a team of "Health Coaches" to specialize in a single disease area (e.g., heart disease, diabetes, etc.). Each Coach will manage a portfolio of patients to reduce the costs of overall health expenditures (e.g., reminders to take drugs, provide limited medical advice, suggested diet, etc.). Studies show that once-a-month contact with each patient reduces health spending by 5%, on average.
prompt.question: Should our client launch the program? If so, what steps should it take?

clarifying_info.a: With spiraling health care costs, the industry is under pressure to innovate new products that will control spending. Assume the client is first to market. Past attempts to purely automate DM have yielded minimal savings.

clarifying_info.q: How do the Health Coaches operate?
clarifying_info.a: All activity is conducted remotely via phone/email. The typical profile is a registered nurse who wants to work from home. It is difficult to actually reach patients, so Coaches can contact 8 members per day (assume 25 days per month).

clarifying_info.q: What does a Health Coach cost?
clarifying_info.a: Annual costs per Coach: $60K salary + 20% other (training, benefits, laptop, etc.). There are no other program costs.

exhibits.title: Client's member segmentation by health condition
exhibits.shows: A chart segmenting the client's 5 million members by plan type (Group, Individual, 65+) and by health condition/disease area, showing the percentage of each segment that falls into various disease categories including diabetes.
exhibits.data: Three segments: Group, Individual, 65+ (Medicare Advantage, premiums funded by government). 65+ segment: 20% of members = 1MM; 40% of 65+ are diabetic = 400,000 diabetics. Individual segment has roughly half the diabetic PMPM cost savings vs 65+. Group segment is the healthiest (youngest, working).

exhibits.title: Average cost data (Per Member Per Month)
exhibits.shows: A table showing average Per Member Per Month (PMPM) costs and a diabetic cost multiplier for each member segment.
exhibits.data: Individual: Average PMPM $150, Diabetic PMPM = 4x average ($600). Group: Average PMPM $100, Diabetic PMPM = 4x average ($400). 65+: Average PMPM $300, Diabetic PMPM = 4x average ($1,200).

framework: Program Savings: Understand customer segmentation by disease area and cost per member to estimate total savings from the 5% reduction
Program Costs: Determine salary and other costs per Coach, and portfolio size/capacity (members per Coach)
Profitability: Compare per-Coach savings vs. per-Coach costs; determine break-even and profit per Coach across segments
Risks: Assess whether key assumptions hold (5% savings, Coach capacity), competitive response, and regulatory/liability considerations

questions.prompt: Which member segment and disease area should the client focus on first?
questions.guidance: The 65+ (Medicare) segment contains the sickest patients, followed by Individual; Group members are youngest and healthiest. Sicker patients drive higher costs, so the 5% savings from DM will have the biggest dollar impact on 65+. Within disease areas, diabetes (Type 2) is the right focus: diabetics make up the largest share of sick members and, as a chronic behavioral disease, they are most likely to respond to coaching interventions.

questions.prompt: How many 65+ diabetics are in the client's member base?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply total members by the 65+ segment share, then by the diabetic share within that segment.

math.setup: Total members = 5,000,000; 65+ segment = 20% of members; diabetic share within 65+ = 40%

questions.prompt: What is the maximum portfolio size for a single Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Use the contact rate and working days to derive maximum patients per Coach per month; one contact per month is required.

math.setup: 8 contacts per day x 25 days per month = maximum patients reachable in a month (each needs 1 contact/month)
steps: Since each patient requires 1 contact per month, max portfolio = 200 patients per Coach

questions.prompt: What is the total annual cost per Health Coach?
questions.guidance: Add base salary to the 20% overhead.

questions.prompt: What are the annual savings generated by one Coach managing a portfolio of 200 65+ diabetics?
questions.guidance: Use the 65+ average PMPM, the diabetic cost multiplier from Exhibit 2, the 5% average savings from the program, and the portfolio size.

math.setup: 65+ average PMPM = $300; diabetic factor = 4x; savings rate = 5%; portfolio = 200 patients; 12 months
steps: Annual savings per patient = $1,200 x 5% x 12 months = $1,200 x 0.05 x 12 = $720
Wait — re-deriving: $1,200 PMPM x 5% = $60/month savings per patient
$720 x 200 patients = $144,000 savings per Coach per year

questions.prompt: What is the profit per Coach for the 65+ diabetic segment, and what is the total annual profit if 2,000 Coaches are deployed?
questions.guidance: Subtract cost from savings per Coach; multiply by total Coaches to get program profit.

math.setup: Savings per Coach = $144,000; Cost per Coach = $72,000; Total Coaches = 2,000
steps: Profit per Coach = $144,000 - $72,000 = $72,000 (a 2x return on Coach cost)
Total program profit = $72,000 x 2,000 Coaches = $144,000,000 = $144M per year
math.answer: $72,000 profit per Coach per year; $144M total program profit per year

questions.prompt: How do the Individual and Group diabetic segments compare in profitability?
questions.guidance: Individual segment PMPM is $150 (half of 65+), so diabetic PMPM = $600. Savings per patient = $600 x 4 x 5% x 12 = $1,440... re-check: $150 x 4 = $600 PMPM diabetic; $600 x 5% = $30/month; $30 x 12 x 200 = $72,000 savings per Coach = exactly equal to cost, so break-even. Group PMPM = $100; diabetic PMPM = $400; $400 x 5% x 12 x 200 = $48,000 savings per Coach vs $72,000 cost — a loss.

math.setup: Individual: PMPM $150 x 4x diabetic factor = $600 diabetic PMPM. Group: PMPM $100 x 4x = $400 diabetic PMPM.
steps: Individual savings per Coach = $600 x 5% x 12 x 200 = $72,000 = exactly equal to cost => break-even
Group savings per Coach = $400 x 5% x 12 x 200 = $48,000 < $72,000 cost => loss of $24,000 per Coach
math.answer: Individual segment: break-even. Group segment: unprofitable ($24,000 loss per Coach per year).

brainstorming.prompt: There are 650K Group diabetics left uncoached. Is there a way to make the Group segment profitable?

categories.name: More efficient DM delivery
ideas: Coaching at the workplace to improve reach rates
Bi-monthly instead of monthly contact to double portfolio size
Automated correspondence (email, app) to supplement live contacts

categories.name: Additional revenue sources
ideas: Employers (Group plan sponsors) might pay a fee for a healthier workforce
Government subsidies or incentives for preventive care programs

categories.name: Better patient targeting
ideas: Since 5% is an average, target Group members most likely to respond with above-average savings
Focus on highest-risk, highest-cost Group diabetics to maximize dollar savings per contact

recommendation: The client should launch the Health Coaching program, initially focused on diabetes in the 65+ Medicare segment
Launch a pilot program first to validate key assumptions (5% cost reduction, Coach portfolio capacity of 200 patients, etc.)
Expand to the full 65+ diabetes segment — at $72,000 profit per Coach this yields a 2x return on each Coach's cost and $144M annual profit with 2,000 Coaches
Consider extending to the Individual diabetes segment despite break-even economics, for customer retention and ethical/moral rationale
risks: The 5% savings assumption may not hold for all patients or all coaches — pilot results are critical
Coach capacity of 200 patients assumes 8 contacts/day; actual reach rates in the field may be lower
Regulatory or liability exposure from nurses providing remote medical advice
Competitive response once competitors observe the program's success
next_steps: Run a controlled pilot to validate the 5% savings and 200-patient portfolio assumptions
Hire and train an initial cohort of Health Coaches for the 65+ diabetes rollout
Develop a business case for the Individual segment incorporating retention value
Explore options (employer fees, automation, targeting) to make the Group segment viable
Evaluate selling the Health Coach service externally to other payers (pricing and regulatory challenges to work through)
